candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — basal insulin glargine administration
candidate.educational_objective: Teach correct basal insulin glargine administration: once-daily subcutaneous dosing at a consistent daily time, without mixing it with other insulins.

options.A: Inject it subcutaneously once daily at any time of day, but at the same time every day
options.B: Use it only as a rapid mealtime bolus when carbohydrate intake is high
options.C: Give it intravenously for acute diabetic ketoacidosis
options.D: Mix it in the same syringe with another insulin before each dose

candidate.rationale: Current LANTUS labeling states that insulin glargine is administered subcutaneously once daily at any time of day, but at the same time each day. It is a long-acting basal insulin rather than a rapid mealtime insulin, it is not recommended for treatment of diabetic ketoacidosis, and the label instructs not to dilute or mix LANTUS with another insulin or solution. Therefore A is the best answer.
candidate.source_claim_supported: LANTUS is a once-daily subcutaneous basal insulin administered at the same time each day; it should not be mixed with other insulin and is not DKA therapy.
candidate.source_locator: §2.1 General Dosing Instructions: administer subcutaneously once daily at any time of day but at the same time every day; do not dilute or mix with other insulin/solution. §1 Limitations of Use: not recommended for treatment of diabetic ketoacidosis
candidate.source_organization: U.S. National Library of Medicine — DailyMed
candidate.stem: A client is prescribed insulin glargine (LANTUS) as basal insulin. Which administration teaching is correct?
